payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the mug positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows the mug positioned to the right of the headphones; fail if it clearly shows the mug is not to their right; unknown if their relative position cannot be determined. For R1, complete if this check passes; absent if it fails and no requested change has progressed; partial if the mug has moved toward the requested position but is not yet to the right; unknown if required evidence remains unresolved. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Compare the mug’s visible position with the headphones in the image. Judge the requested spatial relationship, without requiring a particular editing technique.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the visible mug is positioned to the right of the headphones.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image clearly shows a mug and headphones, and their relative positions are observable: the mug is to the right of the headphones. Both objects are identifiable enough for comparison.

fulfillment: The binding is too broad and the node treats the final spatial relation as sufficient proof of the requested edit. In the edited image, a mug is indeed to the right of the headphones, but the source shows the mug to their left; the edit appears to add/move a mug to the right while leaving a mug-like object on the left, so the requested change has progressed without clearly being completed. Make the criterion compare the same target mug’s position in the source and edited snapshots, and distinguish partial progress from completion when the requested relocation is not unambiguously complete. Do not infer completion from two support observations that repeat the same final-state claim; they are dependent on the same evidence, not independent confirmation. Preserve unknown for genuinely insufficient evidence, and keep transport/schema failures separate from visual evidence—none are reported here.

response.content: {"text":"The binding checks only whether a mug is right of the headphones in the edited snapshot, so it mistakes a final-state relation for completion of the requested relocation. Make the node track the same source mug across snapshots and assess its displacement relative to the headphones; distinguish a completed move from partial progress when the original mug remains or the target’s identity/continuity is ambiguous. Here the source mug is left of the headphones, while the edited image appears to retain a mug on the left and show another on the right, supporting progress but not clearly proving the original mug was moved. Avoid treating the dependent s1/s2 observations as independent confirmation. Keep unknown for genuinely unresolved identity or visibility, and do not conflate visual uncertainty with transport/schema failure (none is reported)."}
